title: Discrete lattice derived invariants via a sheaf-module Koszul resolution
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], let $r\geq0$, and let $P$ be an internal $R$-module [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] equipped with pairwise commuting $R$-linear automorphisms $T_1,\ldots,T_r$. Equivalently $P$ has an action of the discrete group $D=\mathbf Z^r$, whose $i$th basis vector acts as $T_i$. Write $R\Gamma_D$ for the ordinary total right derived functor [def-sfb-right-derived-functor] of invariants on $D$-equivariant internal $R$-modules. Define the cochain complex $K_R(P;T)$ in degrees $0,\ldots,r$ by
$$K_R(P;T)^a=\bigoplus_{I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,r\},\ |I|=a}P,\qquad (dx)_J=\sum_{i\in J}(-1)^{\#\{j\in J:j<i\}}(T_i-1)x_{J\setminus\{i\}}.$$
There is a natural isomorphism
$$\lambda_R:K_R(P;T)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma_D(P)$$
in the ordinary derived category of internal $R$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Its map from $P^D[0]$ is the degree-zero inclusion of invariant elements into $K_R(P;T)^0=P$. For a morphism $\varphi:R\to R'$ of commutative condensed rings, an internal $R'$-module $P'$ with commuting automorphisms $T'_i$, and an $R$-linear equivariant morphism $f:P\to\operatorname{Res}_\varphi P'$ to the scalar restriction [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars] (same underlying internal module, $R$ acting through $\varphi$), the square with rows $\lambda_R,\operatorname{Res}_\varphi\lambda_{R'}$ and columns the termwise map induced by $f$ and the canonical derived coefficient map $R\Gamma_D(P)\to\operatorname{Res}_\varphi R\Gamma_D(P')$ commutes. For $r=0$, $\lambda_R$ is the identity $P[0]$.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal M_R$ be the internal module category and $\mathcal E_R$ its category of $D$-actions. Use [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence] and [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor] to identify internal modules with section-ring module sheaves on the condensed site; the equivalence leaves sections, restrictions and underlying abelian sheaves unchanged. These actions are functors from the one-object category $BD$ to $\mathcal M_R$: a functor assigns to each $v\in D$ its module automorphism. Choose the small coefficient site and universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. By [lem-weil-pbc-small-module-diagrams-grothendieck], with $J=BD$, $\mathcal E_R$ is Grothendieck abelian, hence has enough injectives by [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives]. Invariants are right adjoint to the exact trivial-action functor: a map from a trivial-action module is equivariant exactly when its image is fixed by every $u_i$. Thus invariants are additive and left exact. Choose $P\to I^\bullet$, zero in negative degrees, an equivariant injective resolution in the sense of [def-sp-injective-resolutions].

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-integral-lattice-cubical-contraction]. Replace each integral basis symbol $[v,I]$ by a copy of $R$ and every integral matrix entry by the corresponding multiple of the identity, obtaining $L_a=\bigoplus_{|I|=a}\bigoplus_{v\in D}R$ in $\mathcal E_R$, with translation action, the same boundary and augmentation $L_0\to R$. Each column of every matrix is finite because its image is an element of a free abelian group; the maps therefore exist by the coproduct universal property. The contraction identities remain identities of morphisms. Thus the underlying augmented complex is split exact. This construction also works with any internal module $Q$ in place of $R$, giving the augmented exact complex $\bigoplus_{I,v}Q\to Q$. Exactness is also equivariant: kernels and cokernels of a diagram of module sheaves are computed on its underlying sheaves, by [lem-sfb-internal-action-site-presentation], applied to the constant condensed group $D$. The contraction itself is only nonequivariant, as allowed by the cited algebraic lemma.

proof.text: For equivariantly injective $J$, consider the augmented complex of internal equivariant Hom objects from $L_\bullet$ into $J$, augmented by $J^D$. To check exactness, evaluate on an arbitrary profinite site object $S$. Write $R[S]=j_{S!}R_S$ for the sheafification of $V\mapsto\bigoplus_{V\to S}R(V)$, as in [lem-pc-sites-modules-j-shriek-flat]. The exact tensor comparison [lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison] identifies the internal and sectionwise relative tensors. Its free property and [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed] identify these sections with $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal E_R}(R[S]\otimes_R L_\bullet,J)$, augmented by $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal E_R}(R[S],J)$, where $R[S]$ has trivial action. Tensor commutes with these coproducts since it is a left adjoint. Step 2 with $Q=R[S]$ makes the augmented source complex exact. Applying $\operatorname{Hom}(-,J)$ is exact: extend a map from any image subobject by injectivity; the kernel condition is factorization through the quotient. Thus the augmented section complex is exact for every $S$, hence the augmented sheaf complex is exact. No projectivity of $R[S]$ is required.

source.place: Tags 03EV (lemma-j-shriek-flat), 03DA (lemma-abelian); elementary injectivity argument after the integral contraction.

proof.text: An equivariant map out of the summand indexed by $I$ in $L_a$ is uniquely determined by the image $x_I$ of $[0,I]$; the image of $[v,I]$ must be $T^v x_I$, where $T^v=\prod_iT_i^{v_i}$. This holds after every profinite base change, and therefore identifies internal equivariant Hom with $\bigoplus_{|I|=a}J$ (the index set is finite). Precomposing with $\partial[v,I]$ sends the $i$th term to $(T_i-1)x_{I\setminus\{i\}}$ with exactly the sign in the statement. The augmentation is the inclusion $J^D\to J$. Consequently step 3 says $J^D[0]\to K_R(J;T)$ is a quasi-isomorphism for every equivariantly injective $J$. For arbitrary $P$, the same formula defines $K_R(P;T)$ and $d^2=0$: each pair $i\ne j$ appears twice with opposite signs and commuting factors $(T_i-1)(T_j-1)$.

proof.text: Form $B^{a,b}=K_R(I^b;T)^a$ for $0\leq a\leq r$ and $b\geq0$, with horizontal Koszul differential and vertical resolution differential. They commute because the resolution maps are equivariant. Use $d_{\mathrm{Tot}}=d_h+(-1)^a d_v$ and finite diagonal sums [def-sp-double-complex-total]. Each functor $K^a$ is a finite biproduct of the underlying-module functor, hence exact: kernels and cokernels are computed componentwise on those finite summands. Therefore $P\to I^\bullet$ induces a columnwise quasi-isomorphism from the double complex concentrated in $b=0$ with row $K_R(P;T)$ to $B$. By [lem-sc-first-quadrant-total-column-comparison] it induces a quasi-isomorphism $c_P:K_R(P;T)\to\operatorname{Tot}B$.

Step 4 applied to each $I^b$ gives a rowwise quasi-isomorphism from the double complex concentrated in $a=0$, with column $(I^\bullet)^D$, to $B$. The row variant of [lem-sc-first-quadrant-total-column-comparison] therefore gives a quasi-isomorphism $b_P:(I^\bullet)^D\to\operatorname{Tot}B$. To use its column formulation interchange the indices; multiplication by $(-1)^{ab}$ identifies the two total conventions, since the horizontal and vertical cross signs then agree. This sign is $1$ on the two axes. By [lem-sp-derived-injective-resolution-naturality], $(I^\bullet)^D$ is the normalized model of $R\Gamma_D(P)$. In the ordinary derived category define $\lambda_R=b_P^{-1}c_P$, with this model identification. The square of augmentations from $P^D[0]$ commutes already on complexes: both composites have its invariant element in $I^0$ and zero in all other components. Hence $\lambda_R$ has the required invariant inclusion normalization.

For an equivariant map $P\to Q$, lift it to nonnegative injective resolutions by [lem-weil-pbc-injective-resolution-lift-exists]. It induces a map of the double complexes, and both $b$ and $c$ commute with it termwise. The normalized comparison of [lem-sp-derived-injective-resolution-naturality] identifies the other side with $R\Gamma_D(P\to Q)$. Two lifts are homotopic by [lem-weil-pbc-lift-to-injective-unique-up-to-homotopy]. Applying the finite-sum functors gives a vertical homotopy compatible with the horizontal maps; multiplying its component on $B^{a,b}$ by $(-1)^a$ makes it a total homotopy, because the horizontal terms cancel. The same argument applied to identity maps between two chosen resolutions proves independence of that choice. Thus the isomorphism is natural in equivariant modules.

Let $U=\operatorname{Res}_\varphi$ and take an equivariant $R'$-injective resolution $P'\to J^\bullet$. Restriction is exact: underlying abelian sheaves, kernels and sheafified cokernels are unchanged [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Choose an equivariant $R$-injective resolution $UP'\to I^\bullet$. By [lem-weil-pbc-lift-along-injective-quasi-iso] the monic quasi-isomorphism $UP'[0]\to UJ^\bullet$ admits an extension $\beta:UJ^\bullet\to I^\bullet$ of the latter augmentation. Both resolve $UP'$, so $\beta$ is a quasi-isomorphism. The double complexes $K_R(UJ^b)^a$ and $U K_{R'}(J^b)^a$ are identical: their summands, automorphisms and integer signs are identical. Their augmented rows are quasi-isomorphisms by step 4 over $R'$ and exactness of $U$. The double-complex map induced by $\beta$ is a columnwise quasi-isomorphism, because the finite-sum $K^a$ are exact. Total comparison and the commuting row-augmentation square imply that $\Gamma_D(\beta):U\Gamma_D(J^\bullet)\to\Gamma_D(I^\bullet)$ is a quasi-isomorphism.

The canonical coefficient comparison for $UP'$ is represented by the inverse of $\Gamma_D(\beta)$ in step 8: first map $U\Gamma_D(J^\bullet)$ to $R\Gamma_D(UP')$ by the derived-functor unit on the resolution $UJ^\bullet$, and then invert this comparison, which step 8 proved is an isomorphism. The unit and its naturality here are those of [def-sfb-right-derived-functor]; the computation equation is $c_s\eta_K=Q\Gamma_D(s)$ for a resolution $s:K\to I$. This is the normalized acyclic-resolution definition of the coefficient comparison; on the chosen injective $R$-resolution it uses precisely the extension $\beta$. Changing $\beta$ does not change it: the two extensions agree on $UP'[0]$, so [lem-weil-pbc-lift-to-injective-unique-up-to-homotopy] makes them homotopic, and applying the additive invariants functor preserves that homotopy. The squares for $b,c$ and $K(\beta)$ commute on complexes. Inverting their quasi-isomorphisms gives $U\lambda_{R'}=\text{(coefficient comparison)}\circ\lambda_R$ under the termwise identity $K_R(UP')=UK_{R'}(P')$; the left vertical map here is that identity. Compose with the naturality square of step 7 for $f:P\to UP'$ to obtain exactly the square in the statement. No injectivity of $UJ^b$ over $R$ was assumed.

For $r=0$, the complex $K_R(P;T)$ is $P[0]$ and invariants is the identity functor. The double complex has only the $a=0$ column; the two comparison arrows are respectively $P\to I^\bullet$ and the identity of $I^\bullet$. With the normalized derived identity comparison this gives $\lambda_R=1_{P[0]}$. The zero module and the zero ring cause no exception: all displayed complexes and maps are zero. For $r=1$ the formula is $P\xrightarrow{T_1-1}P$, with invariant inclusion in degree zero, so the augmentation convention has the asserted sign.
